articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Car-Following Model Combining Kinetic Dynamics and Deep Learning Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Car-following (CF) model has been extensively studied from various aspects and by different methods in the past few decades. Moreover, with the help of big data and advanced deep learning technologies, recent work seeks data-driven car-following modeling. Nonetheless, the interpretability and reliability of the data-driven model need to be further addressed. In this paper, we propose a novel hybrid car-following model that combines traditional mathematical kinetic dynamics and a deep learning network, in which the mathematical model is used to statistically describe general human driving behavior and the deep learning network is used to capture the complexity of random driving behavior caused by specific human factors. In particular, we define a general network to train the residual data calculated by the estimated kinetic model and real driving trajectories. Specifically, the typical Intelligent Driving Model (IDM) is adopted as the mathematical model, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network is used as the basic network to build our hybrid model - RES-ILSTM. We compare the calibration and prediction results with several models using the NGSIM dataset to evaluate the proposed model. The experiments show that our calibration algorithm achieves better accuracy of results and RES-ILSTM is able to maintain high modeling accuracy and performs well in terms of interpretability, data efficiency, and generalization.

articleTitle: Research on TACS System Based on Structured Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The train autonomous operation control system (TACS) based on train vehicle communication is gradually applied in the metro and other rail transit fields. It's architecture and information flow are relatively simple, and it's main feature is that it improves the utilization rate of trackside resources, can refine the management of turnout resources and simplify trackside equipment. The structured analysis method is used to collect and analyze the requirements of TACS system, and it is pointed out that this system is a new generation of train operation control system with higher reliability, higher operation efficiency and lower full life cycle cost, which will provide great support for the upgrading of urban rail transit signal system.

articleTitle: The Test Solution for Digital Key of Connected Car Services in Vehicle HILS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method of verification to conveniently verify the Digital key system without Gateway and wireless communication module. We provide the digital key verification environment and functional analyses for the connected car service with virtualization operations over the HTTP protocol. Our simulated results not only show that this system works at an apparently identical level of functionality as compared to the system of vehicles with actual ECUs(Electronic control unit) attached, but also enable in-depth analysis. Furthermore, we show that this system provides data analytics between the ECUs and the server during the MO(Mobile Originated) and MT(Mobile Terminated) communications. We thus believe that the proposed system can be a good framework for the verification of Connected car service.

articleTitle: A Bi-Objective Bi-Level Programming for Connected Bus Lane Reservation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Buses are recognized as a highly efficient mode of transportation, and therefore the reservation of lanes for them is considered to increase the attractiveness of the public transportation system. However, the routes of social vehicles often change due to the choice of dedicated lanes, which leads to dynamic changes in the state of the road network. Therefore, the main focus of this study is on the reservation of dedicated lanes for bus considering user equilibrium. Under the strict control of cost budget, the objective of this paper is to maximize network connectivity and minimize the negative impact on normal traffic due to the reduction of available lanes for social vehicles. We initially introduce a novel bi-objective bi-level programming model. Then, an NSGA-II algorithm is proposed to solve it. The effectiveness of the proposed model and method is verified by conducting a case study.

articleTitle: The Case Study of Dalian Metro Line 3 Signaling System Transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Some of the Chinese subway signaling systems have been in use for more than 20 years, approaching the safe service life of the Urban Rail Transit Signal system, and the existing signal system cannot meet the requirements of tighter, safer and more comfortable train operation due to the growing development of the city and society, therefore, the existing signal system needs to be upgraded. Urban rail transit, as the main infrastructure of a city, carries extremely important functions and needs to avoid delays and interruptions in operation, and the signal system, as the central system for commanding the safe operation of trains in urban rail transit, cannot have any faults that affect normal operation during the transformation process. Based on this, this paper is a case study of signalling system transformation of Dalian Metro Line 3, with a view to providing reference for relevant signal system transformation. [1].

articleTitle: Research on Passenger Trip Classification of Multi-mode Regional Rail Transit System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The multi-mode regional rail transit system (MRRTS) includes railway mode and urban rail transit mode. It has diversified passenger travel demands and complicated travel process. As different modes have separate ticket type, current trip classification is limited in addressing the interconected characteristics. In this paper, the trip classification includes commuter trip familiar with MRRTS, other trip familiar with MRRTS and unfamiliar trip with MRRTS. Moreover, the AFC data is mined to establish a trip classification method in urban rail transit system. In addition, trip classification in the railway system is carried out combined with questionnaire investigation and ticket data. Furthermore, the trip of the Chongqing MRRTS is classified by the proposed method, and the result of trip classification is consistent with the main characteristics of rail transit commuting trips. The study breaks through the independence of different tickets among different modes, which enrich the research of passenger trip classification and is important for the further analysis of passenger path selection in the MRRTS.

articleTitle: A Feature-Based Approach for Organizing Spatial Data of Digital Twin Railway
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In response to the challenge of maintaining consistency in storing and processing geometry and semantics in the spatial data model of digital twin railway, a feature-based railway spatial data model is conducted by analyzing the establishing requirement of the railway spatial data model and combining the linear distribution characteristics of the railway. The focus was on providing a detailed discussion of the feature sets and their interrelationships within the conceptual model. Additionally, package diagrams and class diagrams using UML language to express features, which were employed to construct the logical model, and express the description of railway feature objects. Through comparative analysis, it was demonstrated that this model enables the consistent description of the geometry, location, and semantics of feature objects. It fully expresses the complex relationships present in the geographic world, more aligning with human cognitive laws regarding geographic entities.

articleTitle: Scheme Design Analysis of Aligned Isolation Between a Train Door and a Platform Door in Urban Rail Transit Signaling System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: With development of urban rail transit, interlocking between train doors and platform doors has been gradually achieved under CBTC and FAO modes. This article provides with emphasis the scenario analysis, requirement analysis, scheme design, information flow and interface design among systems for a scheme of aligned isolation between a signaling system and a platform control system as well as a rolling stock system in case of faults of train doors or platform doors or in case of manual isolation or when a platform door or train door has not been properly aligned during opening/closing. This offers reference for operational maintenance and/or design of interlocking schemes of signaling integration for newly-built, existing, and under-construction lines. The scheme has been used in Hangzhou Lines 6 and 7 with a CBTC system as well as Ningbo Line 5 with an FAO system. The customers respond that the application effect of this scheme is good.

articleTitle: Research on Identification Method of Ship Docking Area Based on AIS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In order to better dynamically monitor the navigation and transportation situation of ships and improve the efficiency of ship management, this article uses AIS ship trajectory data and port entry and exit report data to identify and study the ship docking area. Firstly, the data content and structure of water transportation big data were sorted out, providing data support for subsequent efficient calculations; Secondly, perform correlation fusion analysis on maritime data of water transportation and select the optimal route data; Finally, the DBSCAN clustering algorithm is used to identify the type names and electronic fence information of ship docking areas. Partial berthing areas were selected for empirical analysis, and the results showed that the DBSCAN clustering algorithm based on the fusion analysis of AIS data and port entry and exit report data can accurately obtain the names of ship parking areas and their electronic fence information

articleTitle: Applications of Machine Learning in Rail Transit Signalling System and Its Independent Safety Assessment Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Rail transit signalling system is an important equipment to ensure the safe and efficient operation of trains, and independent safety assessment of the system can help identify its potential risks and reduce them to acceptable level. In recent years, machine learning techniques have also been applied in rail transit signalling system. Through a series of literature research, this paper summarizes the application status of machine learning in rail transit signal system, analyze the enhancements and challenges it brings. Finally, we proposed an evaluation method for signalling system applying machine learning to ensure safety and reliability from the perspective of independent safety assessment parties.

articleTitle: Design of a Distributed UAV Traffic Management System for Smart Air Service
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: This paper investigates a UAV smart air travel distributed traffic management system, which includes the Public Smart Air Traffic Service Provider (P-SSP) module, the Enterprise Smart Air Traffic Service Provider (S-SSP) module, and the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Operator Operations Control module. The P-SSP module is responsible for providing management during the strategic, pre-tactical, tactical, and emergency stages of UAV flights. The S-SSP module caters to UAV operators requesting services by providing urban air traffic management services and facilitating information sharing with the P-SSP. The UAV Operator Operational Control module is used to customize the service content of the S-SSP. The design of this system aims to meet the requirements of smart city air traffic development and provide a safe, efficient, and fair traffic management solution for operational scenarios such as urban UAV logistics transportation and instant delivery at a systemic level.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Traffic Factors in Foggy Environment Based on Principal Component Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In many adverse weather conditions, fog can easily lead to a large deviation of drivers' observation of road conditions., resulting in traffic accidents. With the widening of traffic safety research field., it is necessary to carry out in-depth research on the key technologies of traffic accident causation mechanism under foggy environment. In this paper., the calculation., sample processing and principal component selection of principal component analysis method are described in detail., and 14 technical indexes of driver reliability factor., vehicle reliability factor and road reliability factor are determined. According to the analysis of the characteristics of various technical indicators in a foggy environment., some key technical indicators were quantified through experiments., the original data were obtained through investigation., and the sample data were obtained through statistical processing., and the principal component analysis method was used to calculate them., converting multiple linearly correlated indicators into a few linearly independent comprehensive indicator variables. The research results can determine the indicators that have a large contribution rate to driving reliability in foggy environment and the cumulative contribution rate meets the research requirements and provide support for the construction of an autonomous identification and early warning system for vehicles in foggy environment.

articleTitle: Intelligent Traffic Signal Control Strategy Based on Rainbow Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The reasonable control strategy of urban traffic signal can alleviate the congestion at intersections. To improve the learning efficiency and stability of intelligent signal control algorithms, this paper proposes an urban traffic signal control strategy based on the Rainbow algorithm. Based on the classical DQN algorithm, the Rainbow algorithm introduces the Double Q-Network, Noisy Network, Dueling-DQN, and Distribution-DQN into the network structure, and introduces the prioritized experience replay technology and multi-step learning into the algorithm training process. Taking the intersections of Niangre Road and Dangre Road in the Lhasa City as an example, three simulation scenarios are set based on the traffic flow intensity. Three traffic signal control strategies are conducted by using fixed-time signal control algorithm, classical DQN algorithm, and Rainbow algorithm, respectively. Results demonstrate that the Rainbow algorithm can converge quickly and reduce vehicle delay time, queue length effectively.

articleTitle: Research on the Digital Twin Platform and Emergency Response Technology for Rail Transit Operation Emergencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: This article aims to study the digital twin and emergency response technology for rail transit operation emergencies in order to improve the safety and emergency response capabilities of rail transit systems. By establishing a digital twin model, the real-time monitoring and simulation of the operation status of rail transit systems can be achieved, providing accurate decision support. At the same time, emergency response technologies for emergencies, including warning systems, emergency response plans, and emergency rescue measures, are researched to minimize accident losses and ensure passenger safety.

articleTitle: Illuminating Transport and Roads to Reduce Accidents and Lighting Requirements: Exploring the Potential of Glow-in-the-Dark Paint
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Road traffic accidents are a significant global problem, leading to numerous fatalities and injuries each year. Particularly, a substantial portion of these accidents occurs during nighttime driving. This research aims to explore the potential of glow-in-the-dark paint as a practical and cost-effective solution to illuminate transport and roads during nighttime hours. Glow-in-the-dark paints, with their photoluminescent properties, offer the ability to enhance visibility, improve driver awareness, and reduce dependence on traditional lighting infrastructure. In addition, this study provides policy suggestions that include mandating the use of glow paints on vehicles and implementing glow-in-the-dark lane differentiations at historically hazardous junctions. By doing so, we can effectively improve highway nighttime safety while addressing the challenges associated with poor highway lighting and the environmental impact of conventional electricity-based lighting.

articleTitle: Exploring the Acceptance of Robotaxi Technology Among the Elderly Based on an Extended Technology Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In recent years, robotaxi technology has garnered widespread attention and research on a global scale. Many countries and regions are actively exploring and promoting the development and application of robotaxi technology. This study aims to investigate the acceptance of robotaxi technology among older adults. By constructing an extended technology acceptance model that takes into account the characteristics of technology anxiety and resistance to change among the elderly, the study examines the acceptance of robotaxi technology among this population. The results indicate a negative correlation between technology anxiety and perceived usefulness as well as perceived ease of use, with no significant relationship observed with intention to use. Additionally, resistance to change is negatively correlated with intention to use. These findings hold significant implications for promoting the application of robotaxi technology among older adults.

articleTitle: Intelligent Guidance Method and System for Driving Safety in Curves Under Slippery and Low Visibility Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Generally, the speed limit signs are set up in front of curves on highways, and the linear guidance signs are set up at curves to remind drivers to slow down, pay attention to changes in route direction, guide the direction of driving, and improve driving safety. However, in adverse weather conditions, factors such as the visual recognition effect of the sign, the friction performance of the road surface, and the braking performance of the vehicle will change with changes in pavement slipperiness and visibility. Therefore, under adverse weather conditions, the slippery pavement and low visibility can directly affect the driving safety of highway curves. This article conducts research on the methods and systems for inducing safe driving in slippery and low visibility curves. Based on the changes in slipperiness and visibility, different guidance control strategies for curves driving are developed, including automatic adjustment of curves speed limit values, automatic movement of speed limit sign positions, automatic adjustment of curves traffic guidance sign spacing and corners, automatic control of the opening and closing of curves traffic guidance sign LED beads, luminous color, luminous brightness, flashing frequency, etc. The study comprehensively considered two environmental factors that affect the safety of driving on curves, namely pavement slipperiness and visibility, achieving dual dynamic control of dynamic movement of guidance signs and dynamic changes in control strategies, achieving guidance for driving on curves in adverse weather conditions, and improving the safety of driving on curves.

articleTitle: Research on Traffic Congestion Warning Method Based on Data Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: A congestion warning method based on changes in the slope of traffic flow basic maps is proposed to address the research gap in which existing research cannot effectively warn of congestion using interpretable methods in the absence of high-quality observation data. Generally speaking, highway traffic congestion is caused by actual traffic flow exceeding the road capacity. When congestion occurs, there will be significant changes in traffic flow and speed. This article proposes a congestion warning framework (based on the “data+model” framework), which is based on the fact that during the duration before and after congestion occurs, traffic increases sharply and speed decreases sharply. In order to find a stable and reliable warning point, this article first determines the range of speed and flow values before and after congestion by observing actual traffic flow data. At the same time, through data fitting, select an appropriate traffic flow model to describe the basic relationship between the traffic parameters of the selected road section. Then, a congestion warning model based on the slope change of the basic graph was proposed. Finally, within the preliminary warning range determined by historical data, the proposed model is used to identify early warning points and achieve congestion warning. Through verification of actual highway traffic flow data, it was found that the accuracy rate of early warning is as high as 94.44%.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of Autonomous Vehicle Hybridization on Urban Road Network Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Driverless technology has become an indispensable part of future transportation, and in order to study the impact of autonomous vehicles on road network capacity in the future and reveal the mutual influence characteristics of autonomous vehicles and ordinary vehicles, assuming that the autonomous vehicles follow the system-optimal paths and the ordinary vehicles follow the user-optimal paths, we construct a mixed-equilibrium two-layer planning model considering the road section capacity constraints, in which the ordinary vehicles aim at the minimization of the individual travel cost, and the autonomous vehicles aim at the system-optimal goal. The incremental method and MSA (Multiple Sequence Alignment) algorithm are used for traffic allocation, and the validity and feasibility of the model are verified by arithmetic examples. In this paper, the impact of autonomous vehicle market penetration and road network perception coefficient on road network capacity is considered comprehensively. The research results show that under specific network conditions, the road network capacity increases with the increase of the market penetration rate of autonomous cars, and the increase of the road network perception coefficient will cause the road network capacity to show a three-stage change of growth-stability-decline. Through the change rule of road network capacity, it can be seen that driverless cars have a significant impact on the enhancement of urban road network capacity, which in turn can be used to obtain traffic management strategies to improve traffic congestion, enhance road network capacity, and promote traffic intelligence and sustainable development of transportation.

articleTitle: Study on Technology of Automatic Generation of Indoor and Outdoor Interlocking Construction Drawing of Signaling System in Urban Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The preparation of signaling system construction drawing has become a barrier to project site construction due to such characteristics as long time span, great review difficulty, and low working efficiency, etc. With respect to this issue, the paper proposes a systematic way of automatic construction drawing preparation developed on the basis of a diagram element library. The system combines basic configuration data with the diagram element library and makes it possible to export a whole set of indoor or outdoor construction drawing with consideration of interface layout requirements from the user. Good economic benefits may be obtained compared with traditional manual plotting.

articleTitle: Refined Improvement Method of Expressway Safety Facilities Based on Risk Assessment Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: With the continuous development of China's economy and society, the traffic operation of expressway has undergone significant changes, making it difficult for safety facilities including traffic signs, traffic markings, and guardrails to meet the current traffic operation requirements. At the same time, the Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Public Security issued the “Action Plan for Refined Improvement of Highway Safety Facilities and Traffic Order Management” jointly, which requires expressway to enhance their safety protection capabilities and provide scientific and standardized information guidance in April 2022. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of expressway safety facilities scientifically and refine the improvement of expressway safety facilities. Introduce risk assessment model to analyze the risks of expressway accidents based on the traffic operating conditions, design indicators and current status of safety facilities, determine the risk levels of each section of the expressway, conduct high-risk cause analysis, and determine the refinement and improvement methods of expressway safety facilities based on the risk assessment results. Taking a certain expressway as an example, a study on the refinement improvement method of safety facilities based on risk assessment models was conducted, and suggestions for refinement improvement of key road sections were provided, which can provide reference for the refinement improvement of safety facilities on other expressway, finally.

articleTitle: Maximizing Parking Operation Revenue via Joint Control of Channels and Overselling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: With the acceleration of urbanization, the problem of “parking difficulty” has become a key issue that needs to be addressed in cities of all sizes. As a new parking method, reservation-based parking can effectively reduce the waiting time for parking and solve the problem of urban traffic congestion. It is widely used to alleviate parking difficulties. This article proposes a method for obtaining maximum parking revenue. Based on reservation-based parking, big data technology is used for analysis and prediction. By jointly controlling the channel ratio and overselling ratio in the reservation process, the optimal parking utilization rate and economic benefits are achieved from low to high reservation penetration rates. In summary, reservation-based parking, as an important means of solving parking difficulties, not only improves parking efficiency and alleviates urban traffic pressure but can also explore the practice of maximizing revenue using big data technology, contributing to the intelligent and green development of urban transportation.

articleTitle: Traffic Management Optimization Based on Generalized Benders Decomposition(GBD): A Case Study of Traffic Signal Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Traffic signal control and flow management play a pivotal role in maintaining the structured flow and order of urban life. Such challenges, intrinsically complex in nature, become increasingly demanding with the rapid urbanization and growth of cities. Addressing this mixed integer nonlinear programming problem (MINLP) requires advanced optimization techniques. The generalized Benders Decomposition (GBD) algorithm emerges as a potential solution, providing more efficient means of arriving at optimal outcomes. Delving deeper into urban transportation dynamics, we develop a comprehensive linear mixed integer programming model. This model aims to optimize urban rail transit transportation organization, ensuring it aligns with real-world traffic demands. We offer a thorough examination of the model's structural nuances, intricacies, and inherent complexities. Furthermore, the Benders Decomposition algorithm is meticulously tailored to effectively decipher and solve the presented model. Leveraging MATLAB, we conducted simulation experiments, the results of which robustly attest to the algorithm's efficacy and superior performance.

articleTitle: Traffic Flow Data Imputation Based on Feature Fusion Attention Imputation Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: With the construction and development of highway informatization, highway traffic has entered the era of big data. The reliability and validity of data are the basis and prerequisite to ensure the reliable operation for the highway information systems. However, data loss is inevitable due to equipment failure and external factors in the process of data collection. It is important to study the imputation method of traffic data. This paper proposes a traffic flow data imputation method based on Feature Fusion Attentional Imputation Network (FFAI-Net). Traffic data are input as a matrix. After shallow feature extraction, the attention mechanism is used to extract the weights of different features for traffic flow data. The feature fusion model gives adaptive learning weights to different levels of features, and establishes a mapping relationship between missing data and real data. With California highway data PeMS03 as experimental data, the test results show that the proposed FFAI-Net has high accuracy at different missing rates.

articleTitle: Lane Detection Method Based on MCA-UFLD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Lane detection is a key technology in automatic driving systems, and one of the mainstream methods is detection based on segmentation. However, this method requires pixel by pixel segmentation of the image. It cannot demonstrate good real-time and robustness when facing complex scenarios. This paper proposes a lane detection method based on MCA-UFLD network, which defines lane detection as the location selection and classification of predefined row anchors in the row direction. The method greatly improves the detection speed. In this paper, the lightweight network MobileNetV2 is used as the backbone network to reduce the parameters needed by the network and improve the running speed. The coordinate attention (CA) module is introduced into the backbone network, and the location information is embedded to enhance the feature extraction of important lane information and solve the problem of long-distance dependence of lanes. Aiming at the problem that the accuracy of long-distance lane detection is not ideal in some complex scenes, an auxiliary branch of vanishing point detection is added to help identify the position and direction of lanes. In this paper, the proposed network is tested on the lane detection dataset CULane, and the performance is compared with the existing classical lane detection networks. The experimental results show that the F1-measure of the MCA-UFLD network on the CULane dataset reaches 69.36, and the FPS reaches 77.14. Compared with RESA, ERFNet, and UFLD network with ResNet-152 as the backbone, the F1-measure is increased by 0.18, 0.53, and 0.38 percentage points respectively, and the FPS is increased by 23.15, 18.18, and 48.49 respectively.

articleTitle: Detecting the Impacts of Mixed Traffic Flow with Connected Automated and Human-driven vehicles on Safety and Efficiency of Expressway Off-Ramp Areas via the TOPSIS-Entropy Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Most existing the mixed traffic flow with connected automated vehicles (CAVs) and human-driven vehicles (HDVs) on expressway off-ramp areas literature focuses on the possible impacts of CAVs with various penetration rates on the macroscopic traffic flow but neglects the platooning intensity of CAVs and comprehensive evaluation of Safety and Efficiency on expressway off-ramp areas. In this article, we proposed a novel model to detect the characteristics of mixed traffic flow on expressway off-ramp areas via not only taking into account the penetration rate of CAVs but also the platooning intensity of CAVs in the mixed traffic flow. Four car-following pairs of vehicles with different time headway are considered, including CAV-CAV, CAV-HDV, HDV-CAV, HDV-HDV respectively. To evaluate the impacts of the mixed traffic flow for both the safety and efficiency on expressway off-ramp areas, we adopted the TOPSIS (the technique for order performance by similarity to ideal solution) -Entropy method. The results showed that the penetration rates of CAVs have a positive influence both on the traffic Efficiency and safety on expressway off-ramp areas when the traffic demands level is free flow or saturated flow. Furthermore, the traffic efficiency could be improved significantly only if the penetration rate of CAVs reaches over 0.4 in the congested flow. By contrast, the intensity of platoons of CAVs lead to a negative effect in the traffic efficiency and safety on expressway off-ramp areas as the traffic demands increase on the road.

articleTitle: Cross-Country Traffic Sign Understanding via Attention Enhanced Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Traffic signs contain important traffic information. Timely and accurate perception and understanding of traffic sign could be significant for driving safety for intelligent autonomous vehicles. In this study, we prioritize the complex problem of cross country road sign understanding with limited data from only one country. Our proposal consists of unsupervised domain adaptation and attention module for Cross-country Traffic Sign Recognition. Most prevalent methods require large quantity of traffic sign data from different countries and states for cross-country traffic sign understanding which could be nearly infeasible due to difficulties in data acquisition, collection and data privacy policies. By applying Squeeze-and-Excitation attention module enhanced unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA), our work demonstrated quality performance in cross-country traffic sign understanding with only source domain data (Traffic sign samples in China). Experimental results suggest that our model can make accurate inferences on the understanding of cross-country traffic signs. We evaluated its performance using data from different countries, including China, Germany, Iran, etc.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Predefined Performance Platoon Formation Control of Automated Vehicles with Uncertain Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: This paper addresses the fixed-time predefined performance platoon formation control problem of automated vehicles with the consideration of uncertain disturbances. First, a general platoon formation control framework is developed. Then, the transformed errors are designed to make sure the predefined performance requirement is satisfied. Furthermore, the radial basis function neural network is introduced to deal with uncertain disturbances, which accommodates unmodelled dynamics and unknown external disturbances. To this end, the fixed-time stability of the whole closed-loop system is proved theoretically, and simulation results are given to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Competitive Pricing of Rail Container Based On Shipper Selection Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In context of modal shift and the reform of rail freight system, it is important to construct a competitive rail container pricing strategy. This paper regards the shippers on the freight line as bounded rational economic men, analyzes their transport mode choice behaviors on the basis of prospect theory and stochastic utility theory. In addition, an optimization model of rail container pricing is constructed with goals of maximizing the revenues of rail transport and volume of modal shift from road to rail, as well as minimizing the generalized costs of shippers. Finally, the freight data on a main freight lines in western China are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed pricing model. The experimental results show that compared with current rail container transport situation, the application of optimized pricing strategy and subsidy can increase the market share of rail container by 94.87%, and the profit by 68.18%. It also results in a reduction in shippers' expense by 5.73%. All of these prove that our proposed approach has practical and theoretical significance.

articleTitle: Study on Key Technologies in Signaling Systems for Urban Rail Transit Interoperability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: With steady growth of urban rail transit operational scale and gradual maturity of fully automatic train operation, an interoperable signaling system supporting region crossing and line crossing has become a trend to be emphasized in development of future urban rail transit and a focal point for future development of urban rail transit. A study is made herein of the key technologies relied on by design of interoperable signaling systems compared with traditional signaling systems, leading to a summary of technical design requirements of interoperable signaling systems and main principles of key technical design. In the study, design ideas and concepts are raised with respect to interoperable signaling systems and relevant thoughts provided on functional and interface design for implementation of interoperable signaling systems.

articleTitle: Improving Highway Pavement Defect Detection via Swin Transformer Integrated TOOD Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Highway pavement health-condition and maintenance is crucial for traffic safety. Through our investigation, Prevalent methods still can not provide satisfactory results in highway pavement defect detection due to the diversity and complexity of the defects. In order to address the diversity and complexity of defects and enhance the performance and efficiency of highway defect detection, we propose a novel pavement defects detection framework termed HPDD (Highway Pavement Defect Detection)-Net. The proposed model adopts the Swin transformer as the backbone, FPN (Feature Pyramid Networks)as the neck, and the TOOD module as the Bbox_head. HPDD-Net integrates candidate region generation and object classification tasks through task alignment. Compared to prevalent two-staged detection models, our approach offers significant improvements in terms of speed and precision. Experimental results has again proved the effectiveness of our implementation by achieving excellent image classification performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Train Energy-Saving Running Strategy Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Due to its advantages such as convenience and efficiency, urban rail transit is increasingly used in big city. With the development of urban rail transit scale, the accompanying train energy consumption problem cannot be ignored. In this paper, the genetic algorithm is used to obtain the speed curves of each level through an off-line calculation method to optimize the energy-saving operation strategy of the train in order to help ATO(Automatic train operation) which can improve the efficiency of train operation and reduce traction energy consumption.

articleTitle: Parametric Identification of Ship Maneuvering Model Based on Multi-Innovation Unscented Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The mathematical model of ship motion is the core of autonomous navigation systems for unmanned vessels. Obtaining accurate model parameters enables more precise control of ships. This paper proposes a Multi-Innovation Unscented Kalman Filter (MIUKF) and introduces forgetting factors to reduce the correction weight of historical innovation, aiming to improve the identification accuracy of model parameters. Additionally, an indepth investigation is conducted on the influence of different innovation lengths on the identification accuracy. The MIUKF is applied to identify the parameters of an improved ship 2-order nonlinear response model, which includes the time constant of the rudder. This model is obtained by multiplying a 2-order linear response frequency domain model with the frequency domain model of the rudder servo system and introducing nonlinear terms after Laplace inverse transformation. The model parameters are identified using simulation data from a Ziazag test maneuver, and the identified parameters are validated for their generalization capability. The results demonstrate that the identification accuracy of the MIUKF algorithm gradually improves as the innovation length increases. Additionally, it verifies the excellent generalization capability of the identified parameters.

articleTitle: Empirical Study on Influencing Factor of Park&Ride Usage in Tourist Areas Using a Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Park & Ride (P&R) has long been recognized as an effective Transportation Demand Management (TDM) measure for alleviating traffic congestion. However, its usage in tourist areas has remained limited due to a lack of information. This paper presents a field experiment conducted in Kamakura city, Japan, utilizing a mobile application that provides P&R facility and real-time traffic information. The study analyzed the choice behavior between selecting a P&R route or a car-only route, along with the factors influencing this choice, using operation logs and GPS data obtained from the application. The analysis revealed that users tend to opt for routes with lower travel costs and reduced driving time. Interestingly, longer access times, including transfers time and travel time of public transportation and walking time to the destination, did not necessarily decrease the likelihood of selecting the P&R route. This phenomenon may be attributed to the distinctive scenic features of the Kamakura area. The findings suggest that P&R holds significant advantages in tourist areas when coupled with accessible information and competitive package pricing.

articleTitle: A Multi-Trip Customized Bus Network Design Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Customized bus services offer irreplaceable advantages in meeting passengers' diverse travel needs and promoting eco-friendly transportation. It is essential to undertake a scientifically planned and strategically laid-out customized bus operation network to achieve the efficient operation of customized buses. In this study, we address a new multi-trip customized bus network design problem with considering passenger time windows, walking limitations, bus capacity, multi-trip, and stop location decisions to simultaneously minimize customized bus operational cost and maximize the number of passengers served. We formulate it as a mixed-integer linear programming model. Computational results for a case based on the well-known Sioux Falls network verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the model.

articleTitle: Research on Road Surface Slippery State Dynamic Evaluation Model of Long Highway Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The environment of long highway tunnels is relatively closed, and vehicles are prone to traffic accidents when the road surface is wet and slippery. Once an accident occurs, it is difficult to rescue, and it is easy to cause a secondary accident. At present, the evaluation method of tunnel road surface slippery state has low spatial resolution and lacks real-time performance. To achieve a fine perception of tunnel road surface slippery state and improve time and spatial resolution of surface slippery state evaluation, the author proposed a dynamic data collection method and a method of tunnel road slippery state evaluation unit division. The evaluation model of the tunnel road surface slippery state was built based on the K-means clustering algorithm. The author selected the tunnel experimental environment in the Proving Ground for Highway of Ministry of Transportation, and set up controlled experiments under different surface slippery states. The experiment shows that the evaluation model for long highway tunnels’ road surface slippery state proposed in this paper can effectively reflect the actual road surface slippery state.

articleTitle: Parking Management Evolutionary Game Analysis between Government and Bike Sharing Enterprises in the Context of Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Due to the lack of technical guidelines and the lack of effective synergy between the various stakeholders, the problem of haphazard parking of shared bicycles is exceptionally serious and has become one of the urgent problems to be solved in the field of urban transport. Since the government and the bike-sharing enterprises have limited rationality, a model of the evolutionary game between them is constructed to analyse its evolutionary stability, in order to put forward effective management mechanisms and policy suggestions for the problem of indiscriminate parking of shared bicycles. The results show that: (1) The reputation loss caused by the government's failure to regulate has a large impact on the government's decision-making, and the government should fulfil its regulatory responsibility even when the regulatory cost is large, in order to achieve a better co-management effect with the enterprises; (2) When the subsidy is small, the government chooses to regulate, and the bike-sharing enterprise chooses the internet of things technological innovation, and at this time, the co-management effect of both of them reaches the best. Moderate technology financial subsidies have an incentive effect on enterprises to carry out IoT technology innovation to optimise parking management; (3) The government introduces an effective penalty mechanism or takes the lead in parking management, which helps to achieve the goal of minimising the government's financial expenditure and social costs.

articleTitle: Research on Bathtub Models of Urban Traffic with Different Velocity-Density Relation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In recent years, the problem of urban traffic congestion has increasingly become the focus of scholars, but there are few studies on the phenomenon of hypercongestion when the traffic density in the city center is negatively correlated with the traffic flow during rush hours. Bathtub model is a suitable and effective model to simulate traffic congestion under this background, but it develops slowly because of the difficulty in solving partial differential equations and other mathematical problems in bathtub model. In this paper, a continuous scheduling preference bathtub model is constructed under Greenberg’ Relation. Then, the velocity, density, departure rate, arrival rate and cumulative departure are calculated in different periods. Finally, a numerical example is used to analyze the characteristics of each index under the Greenberg’ Relation under the equilibrium state, and a comparative analysis is made with the Greenshields‘ Relation. It is found that the Greenberg’ Relation can better fit the phenomenon of hypercongestion, but it can not describe the process of congestion dissipation well. This study extends the theory of bathtub model.

articleTitle: Research on Hybrid Network Technology of Different Systems Based on Safety Data Transmission of Urban Rail Transit Signalling System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The train-to-ground wireless communication service of the early urban rail transit signalling system mainly uses the WLAN technology based on IEE 802.11g. However, a large number of interference problems are found in many cities during the operation of signalling system, which cannot be solved. As the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) authorizes the 1.8 GHz 20 MHz frequency band to urban rail transit, LTE-M technology can fundamentally solve the co-channel interference problem caused by WLAN technology. In the LTE-M/WLAN hybrid networking technology proposed in this document, WLAN is used to carry CBTC train-to-ground communication services on existing lines and LTE-M is used to build a train-to-ground wireless communication system on new extension lines. Vehicles can run in the WLAN coverage area of the existing line and the LTE coverage area of the extended line, implementing inter-RAT hybrid networking.

articleTitle: Emulative Training System for Interoperability in Urban Rail Transit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Currently, emulative training systems related to urban rail transit in China are mostly of a single-system, single-scenario and single-position manual teaching/appraising mode. The emulative training system for interoperability in urban rail transit is a system developed for technical skill training of metro professionals in response to disadvantages of traditional traffic signaling teaching modes. The system is a result of in-depth research in such aspects as position interlocking training, autonomous system appraisal, trainer fault injection, etc. and aims at satisfying integrated needs in aspects of hands-on training tasks and safety training, and so on, by constructing multi-system interoperable operation, refined management of hands-on teaching equipment, rail transit operation and its intelligentized scenario control, etc.

articleTitle: Scheduling Problem of Modular Autonomous Bus
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In this paper we investigate a new form of automated transit that puts modular vehicles into the operational scenarios of public transportation to overcome the disadvantages of traditional buses, including first and last mile problems, low occupancy, low levels of comfort, accessibility, and flexibility. Modular public transport is composed of several identical vehicle modules, which can be dynamically coupled and separated on various roads in the city. In the dynamic coupling process, individuals can dynamically transfer to the matched vehicle module according to their arrival destination. The bus can also adjust the length of the bus through this dynamic coupling and separation. According to the main characteristics of modular bus, we study the maximum number of passengers that can be served by a certain number of bus modules in a certain time range (morning and evening peak) as the objective function under the condition that passengers can transfer, and build a mixed integer programming model. We performed two sets of numerical experiments and sensitivity analyses to investigate the performance of modular public transport in various configurations. The results of numerical experiments show that the modular bus can transfer dynamically and its capacity can be adjusted.

articleTitle: Decision Model of Lane Changing for Autonomous Vehicles Considering Weather Influence
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Adverse weather conditions have a significant detrimental impact on autonomous driving. Incorrect perception information caused by adverse weather can lead to erroneous inputs in the decision-making module. Therefore, it is crucial to develop a decision-making model that can resist the influence of erroneous information. In this paper, we propose a lane-changing decision model that combines the self-attention mechanism and Deep Q-Network (DQN) to filter out irrelevant data and focus attention on vehicles with higher risks. Through experimental simulations, it is observed that the model effectively avoids collisions and ensures vehicle safety. A comparison with other algorithms demonstrates that even in situations where input data is incorrect, the safety rate of the model remains above 95%.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Aluminum Fin Heat Sinks for Cooling Power Modules in Railway Transportation Control Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: The purpose of this work is to discuss the problem of the low heat dissipation efficiency of the control equipment in rail transit trains. The research aim was to develop a power module for the train control apparatus that makes use of aluminum fin heat sinks. The design of the heat sink was altered to increase the efficiency of heat dissipation by creating a thermal simulation model, and the success of the modification was confirmed. The study provided fresh concepts and techniques for heat sink optimization by analyzing the effects of several parameter indicators in the design of aluminum fin heat sinks on heat dissipation efficiency.

articleTitle: Study on the Accessibility of China's Air Transportation Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: As the most efficient and convenient mode, the development of aviation transportation determines the circulation efficiency and agglomeration capacity of regional economic in China. Therefore, continuously improving the aviation accessibility is an effective way to increase efficiency. This paper aims to put forward the evaluation indexes for aviation accessibility through four dimensions: travel time required, network coverage, flight density and flight balance. Here two models are established: minimum access time model and accessibility level based on TOPSIS. By incorporating route networks and flight schedules into the models, we can objectively evaluate the shortcomings of current air operating, assess the contribution of air transport to passenger travel experience and also city competitiveness improvement. The goal is to further enhance the supply efficiency and quality of air transport, meet the increasingly diverse, personalized, and high-quality demands of travelers and drive social progress.

articleTitle: Lane Detection Method Based on Instance Segmentation of Bi-ATT Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: In order to achieve fast and accurate lane detection without limitations, this paper proposes an instance segmentation lane detection method based on an improved BiseNetV2 network. Firstly, we propose a Bilateral Attention Fusion Network (Bi-Att) that incorporates a lightweight multi-scale feature attention fusion module into the semantic branch of the dual branch network. This module effectively focuses on and aggregates global context information, improving the overall performance. Additionally, a cross-layer fusion module is introduced in the binary segmentation decoding process to recover spatial details lost in high-level feature maps, thereby enhancing semantic segmentation accuracy. Secondly, the Bi-Att network is utilized as the backbone of the LaneNet, a well-known end-to-end lane detection network. Finally, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) clustering method is employed for detecting unlimited lanes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an impressive inference speed of 108.66 FPS, with a MIOU index of 52.9% on the Tusimple dataset, and an accuracy of 94.1%. Comparative analysis against existing detection methods confirms the superior overall performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Using Instance Segmentation Model for Multi-Object Tracking of Motorcycles on Signalized Intersection Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 8th International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Engineering (ICITE)
abstract: Motorcycles are the primary mode of transport in developing Asian countries; however, they are being accused of traffic congestion and accidents in urban areas, especially at signalized intersections. This study examined the recognition and identification of motorcycles on signalized intersection approaches. The study applied YOLOV8 instance segmentation model-a set of contours outlining each vehicle object in the image, a deep learning model for detecting and tracking vehicles, along with the deepsort (Simple Online Realtime Tracking) algorithm-to record the speed and movement path of motorcycles under mixed-traffic conditions in Chiang Mai city, Thailand. The study area presents a diverse array of two-wheeled vehicles. This has led to modifications and increased focus on learning about various types of two-wheeled vehicles model detection, such as motorcycles with passengers, motorcycles with non-helmet riders, delivery motorcycles, motorcycle trailers, and three-wheeled motorcycles (tuk-tuk). The performance of tracking algorithm was well depicted in the results, obtaining mAP and MAPE scores of models by 7.2% and 10.6% respectively for deepsort using data obtained from twelve signalized intersections. Additionally, the results also showed that the significant impact of motorcycle behavior and movement tracking on the traffic flows of intersection approaches. The tracking system's performance exhibited notable enhancements, with a 20.81% increase in Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) and a 7.82% increase in Multiple Object Tracking Precision (MOTP) respectively.
